concept: 24/7 crypto VWAP anchor and session-reset sensitivity
summary: Source-anchored research for 24/7 crypto VWAP anchor and session-reset sensitivity. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Gainium documents an implementation choice that counts crossings only within the same anchor period and does not count a restart as a crossing. This is a useful candidate rule to test when a trading signal could otherwise confuse a reset discontinuity with a price crossing; it is not a demonstrated profitability result. (low confidence)

Reset-relative age matters when assessing VWAP signals: altFINS warns that early-session VWAP has little volume behind it, while TradingView explains that a cumulative VWAP develops more lag toward the session end. Treat these as indicator-mechanics cautions, not evidence of a profitable time-of-day rule. (medium confidence)

Methodological inference: a retrospective swing anchor is not automatically an executable historical signal. If identifying that anchor requires later candles, permit decisions only after the anchor becomes knowable and preserve that availability time. The basis is the selectable AVWAP start point and Freqtrade’s warning that future candles in indicators or signals falsify backtests. (medium confidence)

Methodological recommendation: define the anchor-selection rule, the time the anchor becomes knowable, the reset schedule, and the calculation timezone before evaluating signals. This follows from documented subjective-anchor risk, delayed pivot discovery, and explicit session conventions; it does not identify a profitable anchor or establish a universally best reset. (medium confidence)

Changing the reset definition can change the VWAP line even for the same symbol. Methodological implication: compare prespecified reset definitions while holding the input data and price source fixed, rather than treating the anchor as cosmetic. (medium confidence)

Anchored VWAP starts at a user-selected point rather than necessarily at the session open. Anchor choice is substantive: TradingView documents the selectable start, and TrendSpider warns that incorrect, subjective anchors can distort analysis. (medium confidence)

A rolling time-window VWAP and a VWAP reset at a recurring regional open use different inclusion rules. TradingView describes its rolling variant as a moving time window; HyroTrader also uses the phrase rolling session VWAP for a reference that starts at London hours and resets later. Record the actual inclusion rule rather than relying on the word rolling. (medium confidence)

Crypto has no natural daily open. Session/reset rules therefore form part of the VWAP definition: changing the accumulation boundary can change the line. TradingView explicitly defines its Anchor Period as the reset frequency; a crypto daily boundary must be checked on the actual platform rather than assumed universal. (medium confidence)

Methodological recommendation: freeze the reset schedule, calculation timezone, anchor-selection rule, and anchor-availability rule before evaluation. Compare prespecified alternative boundaries and anchors on identical observations, and report changes in VWAP-side classifications and decisions rather than selecting the visually best anchor afterward. This sensitivity protocol follows from configurable reset boundaries, subjective anchor risk, and future-data bias; the cited sources do not establish an optimal crypto reset. (medium confidence)

A bias check is useful but has limited coverage. Freqtrade compares baseline and sliced backtests for changed values; its documentation warns that untriggered signal types remain unverified and can produce a false-negative result. Methodological inference for VWAP: include reset transitions and every event-anchor type in replay checks rather than treating one clean run as proof for all anchor rules. (low confidence)

Crypto has no official market close that uniquely determines session VWAP. Midnight UTC is a convention, and venue or regional boundaries are alternatives; these sources do not establish an optimal reset for SOL perpetuals. (medium confidence)

For Pine calculations, changing the chart timezone only changes displayed times. Calendar variables use the exchange timezone and time functions default to that timezone unless an explicit timezone is supplied. Reproducibility therefore requires recording the calculation timezone separately from the chart display setting. (low confidence)

For a VWAP anchor tied to a regional local clock, specify the region and its daylight-saving behavior. TradingView documents automatic regional-time adjustment for IANA identifiers; HyroTrader discusses aligning crypto VWAP with relevant sessions or time zones. Methodological implication: a fixed UTC boundary and a regional-clock boundary are distinct specifications. (medium confidence)

Session age affects VWAP responsiveness: LuxAlgo describes greater early-session sensitivity and increasing inertia as volume accumulates. Separately, Gainium documents suppressing an incomplete initial historical period. Methodological implication: report both time since reset and whether the anchored accumulation is complete; they are different startup conditions. (medium confidence)

The egui-charts VWAP issue reports that a cumulative calculation without resets changed as more history loaded, and its later activity describes missing instrument metadata leaving dialog-created VWAP on UTC boundaries. This is an attributed implementation case, not evidence that TradingView or Jupiter has the same fault. Methodological implication: test history-extension invariance after a complete anchor and verify that session metadata reaches the calculation. (low confidence)
